blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the upper end of business writing, two things happen at once: ideas get denser, and prose gets quieter. Good executive writers do not raise their voice on the page. They place their best sentence in the open, rely on the reader to notice it, and trust the structure to carry the argument without shouting.

Parallel structure is an underused tool. "We will protect the core, grow the adjacent, and explore the new" carries more force than the same idea spread across three clumsy sentences. Rhythm is not decoration — it is a form of clarity. A well-rhythmed sentence is easier to remember, easier to repeat, and therefore more likely to travel through the organisation intact.

The other discipline is ruthless editing. The first draft of even a good executive memo is almost always too long by a third. What survives should be the minimum prose required to make the argument, and not a word more. If that feels painful, it is almost always because something unnecessary is being protected on aesthetic rather than argumentative grounds.

items.q: According to the text, what happens to prose at the upper end of business writing?
options: It relies increasingly on decoration
It gets louder and more emphatic
It becomes longer and more detailed
It gets denser in ideas and quieter in voice
items.why: "ideas get denser, and prose gets quieter" — mais densidade de ideias, menos volume de voz.

items.q: Why does parallel structure carry more force, according to the text?
options: A well-rhythmed sentence is easier to remember and repeat
It fills the memo with more words
It signals the writer's seniority
It hides the argument from the reader
items.why: "easier to remember, easier to repeat, and therefore more likely to travel… intact."

items.q: What does the text say about the first draft of a good executive memo?
options: It is usually about the right length
It is too short to make the argument
It should never be edited
It is almost always too long by a third
items.why: "The first draft… is almost always too long by a third."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Rhythm in prose serves clarity, not ornament
The best sentence belongs where the reader will see it early
Cutting words can be the hardest part of writing well
A memo becomes more persuasive the more polished sentences it retains
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende edição implacável — quantidade de frases polidas não é o objetivo, e sim o mínimo necessário.

items.q: The phrase "protected on aesthetic rather than argumentative grounds" suggests that…
options: aesthetics have no place in executive writing
writers keep certain lines because they sound nice, not because they help the argument
arguments should be sacrificed to preserve style
beauty and logic always coincide in good prose
items.why: Inferência: mantemos a frase por vaidade estética, não porque ela sustenta o raciocínio — daí a dor de cortar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte revisando a nota estratégica em voz alta. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, third time. Read it back to me. "The committee should protect the core business, invest carefully in adjacent markets, and it is also important that we look at entirely new areas." No. Hear how it stumbles? The first two clauses march, and then the third one trips over itself.

Let me try again. "Protect the core, grow the adjacent, explore the new." There. Same three ideas, but now they land. If a member of the committee remembers one line from this note tomorrow morning, I want it to be that one — so it has to carry on its own, without me in the room to explain it.

Now the opening paragraph. I have been rather proud of this sentence, which is exactly why it is going. It is elegant, it is well turned, and it does nothing for the argument. Out. The note was two pages; it will be one by the time I send it.

People think editing is about tidying. It is not. It is about deciding what you are willing to lose — and then losing it without flinching.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is wrong with Charlotte's first version of the three-part sentence?
options: It uses vocabulary that is too advanced
It contains a factual error
The third clause breaks the parallel rhythm of the first two
It is too short to be clear
items.why: "the third one trips over itself" — a terceira oração quebra o paralelismo das duas primeiras.

items.q: Why does Charlotte want the committee to remember that one line?
options: Because it lists every point in the note
Because it must carry on its own, without her there to explain it
Because it flatters the committee
Because it is the longest sentence in the note
items.why: "it has to carry on its own, without me in the room to explain it."

items.q: Why is Charlotte cutting the sentence she was proud of?
options: The committee asked her to remove it
It is grammatically incorrect
It is elegant but does nothing for the argument
It repeats a point made elsewhere
items.why: "It is elegant… and it does nothing for the argument. Out." — beleza sem função argumentativa.

items.q: What does Charlotte mean when she says editing is "about deciding what you are willing to lose"?
options: Real editing demands cutting good material, not just tidying it
Editing is mainly about correcting typos
Good editing means keeping every strong idea
Editing should be left to someone else
items.why: Inferência: ela distingue arrumar de editar — editar é sacrificar material bom sem hesitar.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's attitude to her own writing?
options: Indifferent to how the note reads
Disciplined, willing to cut even what she likes
Focused only on making it longer
Sentimental and reluctant to change anything
items.why: Inferência: ela corta a própria frase favorita — postura de edição implacável, não sentimental.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The memo relied on parallel structure to make its three priorities land." Parallel structure means…
options: repeating the same word in every sentence
matching the grammatical form of related items
writing in two columns side by side
using very long, balanced paragraphs
items.why: Estrutura paralela = itens relacionados na mesma forma gramatical, o que dá força e clareza.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A single ___ editing ___ removed a third of the draft without weakening the argument." (pick the term for a round of revision)
options: editing pass
first draft
argumentative ground
aesthetic indulgence
items.why: Editing pass = uma rodada de revisão do texto.

items.q: Ruthless editing is best described as…
options: delegating the revision to a junior writer
adding detail wherever the reader might have questions
polishing the wording while keeping the length
cutting without mercy anything that does not earn its place
items.why: Edição implacável = cortar sem dó o que não se justifica no argumento.

items.q: "She kept the line for its beauty alone — pure aesthetic indulgence." This means…
options: keeping something only because it sounds pleasing
a clear improvement to the argument
a standard editing technique
a deliberate factual choice
items.why: Indulgência estética = manter algo só pela beleza, não pela função no raciocínio.

items.q: "A well-rhythmed line is more likely to travel intact through the organisation." To travel intact means…
options: to be filed and archived
to move around while keeping its exact meaning
to be translated into other languages
to reach only senior leaders
items.why: Circular sem distorção: a frase é repetida sem perder o sentido original.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem quando se escreve e se aprova documentos executivos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The chair still has to sign off on the final note before it circulates." To sign off on means to…
options: rewrite from scratch
comment informally
postpone indefinitely
formally approve
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Charlotte had to pare down the memo from two pages to one." To pare down means to…
options: reduce it to the essentials
circulate it widely
add supporting detail
read it aloud
items.why: Pare down = enxugar, reduzir ao essencial.

items.q: "A crisp three-part sentence can move the needle on how a proposal is received." This means it can…
options: make a noticeable difference
confuse the committee
take longer to write
delay the decision
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "The team agreed to shorten the paper but never followed through." They…
options: carried the plan to completion
rewrote it entirely
failed to carry it to completion
sent it to the wrong committee
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "Don't bury the lead at the end — put your best sentence up front." To bury the lead means to…
options: repeat the conclusion twice
delete the opening paragraph
hide the most important point where it is easily missed
state the main point too early
items.why: Bury the lead = esconder o ponto principal em vez de colocá-lo em destaque logo no início.
